title: Auto Loans: the checking ledger balance limits an installment catch-up payment
content:
# Auto Loans: the checking ledger balance limits an installment catch-up payment

This rule of the Auto Loans product category at PCB applies when a borrower pays the earliest past-due installment of an auto loan by a transfer from the borrower's own PCB checking account. It sets how much the transfer draws.

## Clause

The transfer is drawn only from posted money. The paying account is the borrower's PCB checking account in active status. When that account's ledger balance is lower than the installment remainder still unpaid on that installment, the payment is that ledger balance; otherwise the payment is the installment remainder. The payment figure is rounded to the cent. Because every part of the later split is taken from this payment figure, the checking ledger balance drives the whole split.

## Condition, judgement, outcome

| Active checking ledger balance compared with the installment remainder | Payment drawn |
|---|---|
| lower | the whole ledger balance |
| equal | the installment remainder |
| higher | the installment remainder |

## Hypothetical cases (installment remainder 486.20)

| Ledger balance of the active checking account | Payment drawn | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 312.40 | 312.40 | the balance is lower than the remainder |
| 486.20 | 486.20 | equal is not lower, so the remainder is drawn |
| 1500.00 | 486.20 | the remainder is drawn, never more |

## Points of judgement

**Can the transfer take more than the installment remainder to pay ahead?** No. The draw is the installment remainder at most.

**Which checking account is read?** The borrower's PCB checking account in active status; its ledger balance, meaning posted money, is what limits the draw.
